name: Snare
description: A cord drawn tight. The weapon it belongs to does not throw anything and does not land on anything, so the one impact sound in the set would have been a lie — what actually happens is that something is caught and held, and the sound of that is tension arriving rather than a blow. Three voices say it in order. `fibres` is the cord itself taking the strain: nine grains of noise scattered unevenly across two tenths of a second under a bandpass climbing from `$shell` to `$grit`, so the strands give one after another and higher each time, which is the whole of the dry creak the thing is named for. Evenly spaced grains would read as a ratchet, and a ratchet is a machine. `pull` is the body under them, a sawtooth sliding up from `$moan` to `$tap` and shut in by a lowpass — nothing in this weapon is bright, and an unfiltered saw here would put the cord somewhere metallic. It sits in the mids rather than down at `$dirge` where it was first written, because a phone speaker hands back nothing under about 200Hz and a sound whose body lives there arrives on a phone as the grains alone. `cinch` lands last and alone, one short low knock at the moment it stops moving, because a cord pulled tight ends on a stop rather than on a fade. The jitter is on frequency only and narrow: this fires up to three times a cast and a dozen times a fight, and a sound that wanders far at that rate stops being one object.
